notes: Page 2 is a generic introduction (open the box, sort the pieces, start building). No pieces are placed, so nothing is added.

Assumed layout: the two 1x1 bricks sit on the back row of the 4x4 plate (one at each end), and the jumper plate fills the two cells between them. The picture is a bit ambiguous about the exact columns.
The sub-assembly is a small cannon: round plates stacked sideways on the clip of the white clip plate (63868), then the whole thing is placed on the white base.
Assumed: the clip plate rests on the jumper plate b4 only. The order of the round plates (2 white, then 2 black) is a guess from the two small pictures.
The round plates are held sideways, so they rest on nothing below them (rests_on is empty).

Step 3: the jumper plate goes on the free stud of the clip plate b5, which makes the cannon stack as tall as one brick. The two black 1x2 plates go on the base plate b1. I placed them in the front row, side by side, so they can carry the four headlight bricks.

Step 4: the white 1x4 brick lies along the back row on top of brick b2, the jumper b10 and brick b3. The four headlight bricks sit on the black plates, two on each. The two grey 22885 bricks sit on b1, one at each side, with their side studs facing out.
The exact columns and rows for the black plates and the grey bricks are a best guess from small pictures, so check them against the next pages.

The 1x4 print brick sits on the four headlight bricks across the front row. The utility-belt tile is laid on top of that brick. Where the tile goes is a guess, because the picture is small and the tile could sit elsewhere on the front.

The two red round 2x2 bricks are stacked in the middle of the model (the green arrows show one on top of the other). I placed the lower one on the base plate b1, in the free centre cells between the grey bricks, the white back brick and the front print brick. That position is an assumption.

Two black 2x4 plates cover the top of the cube, one on the left and one on the right, with the red round bricks showing between them. The page shows only one of them floating, and it is hard to tell which pieces each plate clutches.

I assumed each plate (long side front-to-back) rests on the white back brick b13, the grey brick on its side (b18 left, b19 right) and the front print brick b20. The tile b21 and the red round bricks may in fact be arranged differently, so check this against the next pages.

Two small sub-assemblies are built (left and right), each a black 2x2 plate with a white 1x2 plate on one half and a clip plate on the other. Each is then pressed sideways onto the four side studs of the grey 22885 brick on that side of the model.

The two clip pieces in the parts box are small pictures. I read the left one as the 1x2 clip-on-side plate 11476 and the right one (one stud plus a clip) as the 1x1 clip plate 4081b. These two readings are guesses.
The sub-assembly plates rest on nothing underneath. They are held only by the side studs.

The six 22885 bricks (5 grey, 1 red) form a hollow ring around the 4x4 top, standing on the two black 2x4 plates. Two grey bricks run along the left edge, two along the right edge, one grey brick sits at the back and the red one at the front.
Their side studs face outwards. The red brick's position (front, facing the viewer) is read from the picture, and the exact row and column of each brick is a guess.

The tower is built first: a green 2x2 brick on another green one, then the yellow round plate, then the pink 2x2 brick on top. The tower is then lowered into the 2x2 hollow in the middle of the ring of side-stud bricks.

I assumed the lower green brick rests on the black plates b24 and b25 under the hollow. This conflicts with the red round bricks b22 and b23 I placed in the centre on step 5. Those two may really sit elsewhere.

Step 10: six more grey 22885 bricks make a second ring, each sitting directly on the brick below it in the first ring (b32 to b37). The red brick at the front stays visible in the picture, so the front brick of this ring is grey and sits above it. The pink brick shows in the hollow middle.
Step 11: a black 4x4 plate covers the whole ring. It is a different plate from the white 4x4 base b1. The parts list shows two 4x4 plates, one black and one white.

The two brown 2x3 plates (the green arrows) press sideways onto side studs on the front face, one on each side of the narrow red strip. The picture does not make clear exactly which bricks each plate grips, so I joined both to the red brick b37 and the grey brick b47 above it.
The black 1x4 plate special 92593 is shown only in the parts box and I cannot see where it goes. I attached it to b47 as a placeholder. It may belong on a later page. Check this against page 13.

This page has no arrows: the three brown pieces (2x4 tile, 1x4 tile and 1x4 plate with 2 studs) are added together on the brown plates b49 and b50 on the side of the model. They cover the plate studs, leaving the two studs of the 1x4 plate showing at the edge.
I do not know the exact grid positions of these three pieces on the 3x4 brown surface, so the joins to b49 and b50 are my best guess. Because they are attached sideways, rests_on is empty.
The two round eye tiles go on the two studs of the brown 1x4 stud plate b54, one on each stud. The studs face outwards, so the eyes sit on the side face of the head.
The curved arrows only mean the model is turned around. The new pieces go on the back of the head.
Parts box: black 2x4 plate, black 1x2 tile, brown 1x2 plate and a brown tile that I read as the 2x2 tile 3068b (the brown piece looks square).

The black 2x4 plate presses onto the back side studs of the grey bricks b36 and b46. The black 1x2 tile covers two of its studs. The brown plate and tile are guessed to be the hair at the back and edge. Their exact positions are not clear from the picture.
One brown 30° sloped brick 1x2 goes on the brown 1x2 plate b59 at the back of the head. I assumed it clutches only b59.

The curved arrows only mean the model is turned around. Two black 2x4 plates are pressed onto the side studs of the right side of the head, each spanning a lower grey brick and the one above it (b34 with b44 and b35 with b45).
Which two bricks each plate spans is read from the picture and could be off by one column.

The picture shows the plate with studs in the upper half and the smooth tile in the lower half of one 4x4 side face. I took this to be the left side, with the four bricks b32 and b33 (lower) and b42 and b43 (upper).
Which of the two pieces goes on the upper and which on the lower row is read from the picture, so it may be wrong.

The curved arrows only mean the model is turned around. The four pieces in the parts box are the same four as in step 15, so this step builds the other (mirror) side of the head and hair in the same way.

All the side-stud faces I can see are already taken by earlier plates (b57, b62, b63, b64, b65). So I could not find a clean place for the black 2x4 plate b66 and I joined it to b64 as a placeholder. The exact positions of these four pieces are a guess, so check them against the next pages.
One brown 30° sloped brick 1x2 goes on the brown 1x2 plate b68, mirroring step 16 (b61 on b59). I assumed it clutches only b68.

The curved arrows mean the model is turned over so the white base b1 and the white print brick face up. The white 2x2 plate goes onto the free 2x2 of studs in the middle of b1. I assumed it clutches only b1.
The picture shows only the final result in the middle of the white top, so which studs the plate uses is a guess.

The 4x box means this small sub-assembly is built four times: a black headlight brick with a white 1x1 tile pressed on its side stud. All four are then placed on the four corners of the turned-over top (the white base b1).
The corner cells are assumed to be free studs on b1. I could not check this against the earlier pieces, so rests_on lists only b1.

The 2x box means two white 1x2 plates. The picture shows one coming down onto two neighbouring headlight bricks, so I took the second plate to go on the other pair. Which two headlights form each pair is a guess (b72 with b73 and b74 with b75).

The page builds a small blaster from five parts: a white round plate, a white clip tile, a white cone, the black gun and a black round plate. The picture is too small to see the order or which piece joins which. My reading is: white round plate into the gun socket, cone on that, black round plate on the cone, then the clip tile on the gun.
The last arrow attaches the whole blaster to the front-lower side of the model. I guessed it clips onto the side clip plate b28. Check this against the next pages.

A new display base is built from the black 6x6 plate. The Brickheadz print tile 2x4 goes at the front, the black 1x4 tile behind it and the black 1x4 plate with 2 studs behind that. The black 2x4 tile (the red arrows) covers the back rows. All four sit on the 6x6 plate only.

The picture shows the finished base with the figure standing on it, but the figure itself is not placed on this page. Its connection to the base is probably on the next page. The order of the rows is read from the picture and could be wrong.
Promotional page for the BrickHeadz range (Finn 41485 and Captain Phasma 41486). No pieces are placed.
Two white 1x2 tiles with groove (lego-3069b) are still unplaced in the parts list. I could not place them on any earlier page, so they may be spare or used on a page I misread.
Last page: a product-feedback competition and the legal text. It has no building step, so no pieces are added.
Two white 1x2 tiles with groove (lego-3069b) from the parts list were never placed, so they are probably spare pieces or belong to a step I could not read.

The two separate groups were the Finn figure (starting at b1) and the display base (starting at b87). The booklet builds one model: the last picture on page 25 shows the figure standing on the base. The figure's two white 1x2 foot plates (b80 and b81, on the headlight-brick legs) are pressed onto the free studs of the black 6x6 plate b87. No piece is added.
The two feet go on the studs between the print tile and the 2x4 tile at the back of the base. That is a best guess from the small picture. Pages 26 and 28 are advertising, so nothing else was added.
